angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 653,958 km at 101.13 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.8885 +/- 0.0116 mas (same row, RUWE 0.95): 101.13 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.94 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract): 653,958 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.99 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5534 +/- 100 K from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2260 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2260.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.487, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
